title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 72
paragraphs: Afterwards, when the year comes round again, they do as follows. They take the most capable of the remaining servants—these are native Scythians, for whoever the king himself commands serves him, and his servants are not bought for money. Of these attendants they strangle fifty, and also fifty of the finest horses; and when they have taken out their bowels and cleansed the belly, they fill it with chaff and sew it together again. Then they set the half of a wheel upon two stakes with the hollow side upwards, and the other half of the wheel upon two more stakes, and fix a number of these in this manner. After this they run thick stakes through the length of the horses as far as the necks and mount them on the wheels; the front pieces of wheel support the horses' shoulders, while those behind bear up their bellies, going by the side of the thighs; and both front and hind legs hang in the air. On the horses they put bridles and bits, stretching the bridles tight in front of them and tying them to pegs. And of the fifty young men who have been strangled they mount each on his horse, having first run a straight stake through each body along the spine up to the neck; a part of this stake projects below, and they fasten it into a socket made in the other stake that runs through the horse. Having set horsemen such as I have described in a circle round the tomb, they ride away.
